To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the concept of text similarity is well grounded and can be used as a basis for a wide range of applications, and that (2) the best way to measure text similarity is a combination of multiple measures.
text similarity is a multi-dimensional task, and that a combination of multiple similarity measures is required for best results.

text similarity measures are a valuable tool in many NLP tasks, that they are not a panacea for all text comparison tasks, and that they are not as simple to develop and evaluate as previously thought.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the definition of the task of computing text similarity, the analysis of existing measures, the design and evaluation of a novel system and the provision of a software package that facilitates future work on the topic.
the definition of a well-founded task and the analysis of the state of the art in text similarity measures.
providing a comprehensive analysis of the task of text similarity, with a focus on its application in the area of text reuse detection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many ways to compute text similarity and there is no single best method.
there is no such thing as the best text similarity measure, but that the best text similarity measures are the ones that are tailored to the application at hand.
the notion of text (similarity) has been studied from various perspectives, and that there is no single best measure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a thorough analysis of the text similarity task and its evaluation and have shown how the results of such an analysis can be leveraged to develop state-of-the-art methods.
we provide a solid foundation for text similarity research and that we provide an open source software framework to support future work.
text similarity is an interesting and important problem in natural language processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a clear need to unify the various text similarity measures proposed in the literature and to make them available as a toolkit for future research.
the development of text measures is an interdisciplinary task, which requires a thorough understanding of both text similarity as well as the evaluation setting.
the notion of text-similarity is much more complex than previously assumed.
